NoteTexAccessor::standardize_summations¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::standardize_summations() const

Collapse \sumlimits/\sumnolimits To \sum¶

standardize_summations() rewrites the literal commands \sumlimits and \sumnolimits to the plain \sum. Use it to normalize summation notation before comparing or diffing math source; a plain \sum is already left as-is, and \sum\limits/\sum\nolimits (the command and the limit-position modifier written as two separate control words) are not matched here — use standardize_limits for that spelling.

The match is a literal substring replacement, not a word-boundary-aware regex: \sumlimits and \sumnolimits are matched and replaced wherever they occur, with no lookahead or lookbehind. Both spellings are replaced in the same pass, \sumnolimits first has no effect on \sumlimits occurrences and vice versa since neither is a substring of the other’s match position in this implementation.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Both Spellings¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"\\sumlimits_{i=1}^n i \\sumnolimits_j j"})
              .tex().standardize_summations()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\\sum_{i=1}^n i \\sum_j j"]

Example 2: A Shape-Preserving Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"\\sumlimits", "no change"})
              .tex().standardize_summations()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["\\sum", "no change"]

Example 3: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().standardize_summations().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().standardize_summations();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • standardize_limits: strip the separately spelled \limits/\nolimits modifier from \sum, \int, and similar commands.

  • standardize_integrals: the equivalent collapse for multi-integral command spellings.
